title: Q3 Music Earnings Roundup: Here’s What Every Company Made (Updating)
summary: A rundown of publicly traded companies’ results for the quarter ending Sept. 30, from Spotify to Universal Music Group and more.
contentText:
Related

-

Dan Rys

-

SiriusXM focused on stabilizing self-pay subscriptions (+5,000 net adds) and driving down churn to 1.5%, while Universal Music Group (UMG) honed in on integrating Downtown Music Group and reviving its subscription and streaming revenue. UMG’s efforts paid off, as the company reported that revenue from subscriptions and streaming grew by 8.4% on an organic basis and 17.9% when including Downtown’s contribution.

Nonetheless, all of these companies are keeping a watchful eye on operating expenses. SiriusXM slashed market spend to make up for revenue stagnation, and UMG recently rolled out another raft of layoffs related to a previously announced cost-cutting plan meant to deliver 250 million euros ($271 million) in annual savings by the end of 2026.

Next week, Sony Group, Sphere Entertainment Company, Madison Square Garden Entertainment, Reservoir Media and SM Entertainment report earnings, among others.

Here is a roundup of the key takeaways from companies’ earnings so far. We will update this list as more results are reported.
